extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for handling ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including hearings, interviews, duty of disclosure, handling of claims after Board decisions, notification of related proceedings, and merging copending reexams.

rubrics_metrics.name: No substitute examiner's answer except on remand
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute examiner’s answer is not permitted unless the reexamination proceeding has been remanded by the Board or Director for such purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on filing a substitute examiner’s answer except when remand by the Board or Director authorizes it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request timing, fee, and participation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant (patent owner) desires an oral hearing, appellant must file a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(3) within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appellant will be permitted to participate in an oral hearing unless he or she has requested an oral hearing and submitted the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(3). See 37 CFR 41.73(b) for the non-extendable two-month deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to close oral hearing to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless the appellant (A) petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 that the hearing not be open to the public, (B) presents sufficient reasons for such a request, (C) pays the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(a), and (D) the petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must meet all four requirements (petition, sufficient reasons, fee, and grant) for a hearing to be closed to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims objected-to-as-allowable treated as rejected when based on rejected amended/new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims indicated as allowable but objected to prior to appeal because of their dependency from rejected new or amended claims will be treated as if they were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims with allowable subject matter but based on rejected new or amended claims are to be “objected to” and handled similarly to applications (see MPEP §1214.06). Allowable dependent claims based on an unamended patent claim that has been rejected, canceled, or not subject to reexamination should not be objected to or rejected because of dependency. See MPEP §2260.01 and subsection II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when Board affirms rejection and no claims stand allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board affirms a rejection of amended patent claim(s) and no further appeal is filed (time for further appeal expired), the examiner should prepare a “Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate” (NIRC) indicating cancellation of claims that do not stand allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) If amended claim 1 is rejected and dependent claim 2 was objected-to-as-allowable because of dependency on 1, and the Board affirms rejection of 1, examiner should prepare NIRC indicating claims 1 and 2 are canceled. (B) If all claims are rejected, examiner may either (1) convert dependent claims into independent form by examiner’s amendment, cancel all claims in which rejection was affirmed, and prepare the NIRC; or (2) set a 1‑month time limit for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.550(c) will not be permitted. If no timely reply is received, prepare NIRC indicating all claims are canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when Board decision yields some claims allowed (prepare NIRC indicating status)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner is sustained in whole or in part but some claims stand allowed, the examiner prepares the NIRC indicating which claims stand allowed (confirmed/patentable) and which claims are canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) If independent claim 3 was allowed and Board affirms rejection of amended claim 1 which caused dependent claim 2 to be objectionable, issue NIRC with claims 1 and 2 canceled and claim 3 confirmed. (B) If Board reverses rejections against a dependent claim but affirms rejection of its parent independent claim, the examiner may (1) convert the dependent claim into independent form by examiner’s amendment, cancel the affirmed claim and issue NIRC reflecting statuses; or (2) set a 1‑month time limit for appellant to rewrite the dependent claim in independent form (no extensions permitted), and if no timely reply, cancel affected claims and issue NIRC accordingly. Similar handling applies to unamended patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review and third-party limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner not satisfied with the Board decision may appeal to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 141; a third party requester of an ex parte reexamination may not seek judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal rights depend on statutory versions and filing/commencement dates; courts have permitted intervention by third party requesters in appropriate circumstances but an intervening third party has no standing to appeal the court's decision (see cases cited: Yuasa Battery; In re Etter; Reed v. Quigg; Boeing Co. v. Comm’r). See MPEP §§1216 et seq. for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor and disclosure in reexamination (37 CFR 1.555(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding. The individuals include the patent owner, each attorney or agent who represents the patent owner, and every other individual substantively involved on behalf of the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty exists with respect to each claim pending in the proceeding until the claim is canceled. Disclosure of information material to a canceled claim is not required if it is not material to any remaining claim. Duty is satisfied if all information known to be material after issuance of the reexamination certificate was cited by the Office or submitted in an IDS. Fraud, bad faith, or intentional misconduct in disclosure means noncompliance. Questions of compliance raised during proceeding are noted as unresolved under §1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'information material to patentability' in reexamination (37 CFR 1.555(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material if it is not cumulative and either (1) it is a patent or printed publication that establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing an Office argument of unpatentability or in asserting patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of the evidence standard, giving each term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and before considering any contrary evidence submitted to establish patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and form of information disclosure statement (IDS) in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information disclosure statement must be filed with the items listed in §1.98(a) as applied to individuals associated with the patent owner, and should be filed within two months of the date of the order for reexamination, or as soon thereafter as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed after the order and before the first action on the merits may be submitted as part of a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 (and may include discussion of patentability issues), or as a separate paper which must be limited to a listing of the information disclosed and an explanation of its relevance. If filed as a separate paper, discussion of patentability issues is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required copies for documents cited in IDS (37 CFR 1.98(a) compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with 37 CFR 1.98(a) as to documents cited in the patent or its parent applications, the party must supply legible copies as required by 1.98(a)(2): (1) each foreign patent; (2) each publication or the portion which caused it to be listed, other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office; (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawing or the portion causing it to be listed; (4) all other information or the portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception in 1.98(d) does not apply to ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings. Parties should provide copies (or required portions) to avoid rejection of the submission on formal grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may satisfy the duty of disclosure and when
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual in a reexamination proceeding may satisfy the duty by disclosing the information to the attorney or agent having responsibility for the reexamination proceeding or to a patent owner acting in their own behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney, agent, or patent owner who receives such information has no duty to submit it if it is not material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding. Responsibility for compliance rests on all designated individuals; failure to comply risks diminishing the quality and reliability of the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews in ex parte reexamination: who, where, and when
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiners and patent owners (or their attorneys/agents of record) must be conducted in the Office at times within Office hours as designated by examiners; interviews are not permitted at any other time/place without Director authority. Interviews for discussion of patentability will not be conducted prior to the first official action except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be arranged in advance. Requests that reexamination requesters participate or attend interviews will not be granted. Telephonic and videoconferencing interviews are permitted according to MPEP §713.01 guidelines. Where a panel review was conducted, panel members should, if practicable, be present at an interview requested to discuss that action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content, timing, and consequences of patent owner's interview statement
rubrics_metrics.description: In every interview with an examiner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the patent owner. The written statement must be filed as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action or as a separate paper within one month from the date of the interview, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written statement requirement cannot be waived by the examiner. Failure to file the written statement as required under 37 CFR 1.560(b) will result in termination of the reexamination prosecution under 37 CFR 1.550(d) (analogous to failure to timely respond to an Office action). An interview does not remove the necessity for response to Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview procedures: pre-interview materials, duration, limitations on frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: If patent owner desires to initiate an interview, contact examiner and, if interview granted, file at least three working days prior an informal written statement of issues to be discussed and an informal copy of any proposed claims (unless waived). Duration of the interview will not exceed one hour unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 shows sufficient cause for more time. Only one interview may be requested after an Office action and prior to filing the response to that action, absent good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary materials (fax or hand-carried) help structure the interview and are made of record as attachments to the Interview Summary form PTOL-474. Examiner may extend interview duration at examiner’s discretion. A second interview requires showing of good cause explaining why the information could not have been presented sooner, mindful of the statutory mandate for 'special dispatch.' See MPEP §713.09 for standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording interviews and notifying third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete an Ex Parte Interview Summary form PTOL-474 for each interview where a matter of substance has been discussed; a copy should be given to the patent owner, the original made of record in the reexamination file, and a copy mailed to any third party requester and the patent owner if not already provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General procedures for conducting and recording interviews are described at MPEP §§713.01–713.04. Informal copies considered by the examiner will be made of record as attachments to PTOL-474.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on communications with parties other than the patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any party who is not the patent owner requests information as to the merits of a reexamination proceeding, the examiner will not conduct an interview with that party to provide such information; only questions on strictly procedural matters (i.e., any information obtainable by reading the public file) may be discussed with that party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines: (A) any information obtainable by reading the file is procedural and may be discussed only to the extent of the information in the public file; (B) a matter not available from the file is considered to relate to the merits and may not be discussed. Examples: timing of next Office action and claim interpretation beyond quoting an Office action are merits and must not be further discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding, the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (e.g., interferences, reissues, ex parte reexaminations, inter partes reexaminations, litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement includes supplemental examination and PTAB reviews. While ordinarily no third-party submissions after the order are entered, the Office will accept copies of notices of suits and decisions to ensure a complete file. Submissions must be limited to notification (no additional arguments). Highlighting text or including arguments will cause the submission to be returned, expunged, or discarded. If the Office deems a submission too voluminous, it may return/expunge at its discretion; party may resubmit a limited set. Proper submissions will be entered into reexamination file and considered at the next action on the merits. Form paragraphs 22.07 and 22.08 may be used to remind parties of continuing duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple copending ex parte reexamination requests: substantial new question and merger policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If ex parte reexamination is ordered while a prior ex parte reexamination proceeding is pending and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not been terminated, the ex parte reexamination proceedings will usually be merged and result in the issuance and publication of a single certificate under §1.570. For a second or subsequent request to be granted, a substantial new question of patentability must be raised by the art cited in the later request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision whether to combine proceedings will be made by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Director (or delegate). No decision on combining should be made until reexamination is actually ordered in the later request. If proceedings are merged, prosecution continues at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding. If a final rejection had been issued in the first proceeding, prosecution will ordinarily be reopened where any new patents or printed publications presented in the second request are applied in a new ground of rejection. The patent owner will be provided an opportunity to respond to any new rejection in a merged proceeding prior to final action. A single certificate will be issued based upon merged proceedings.
